mainTopic: The קטורת procedure inside קודש הקדשים, and whether a replacement כהן גדול may use the blood of a פר his predecessor slaughtered, with challenges from פסח and פטר חמור.
overview: This amud opens with a ברייתא describing how the כהן גדול, inside קודש הקדשים on יום הכיפורים, moves the קטורת from the ladle back into his cupped hands. It then records a dispute over whether he heaps the קטורת on the coals or scatters it. The ברייתא calls this the hardest עבודה in the מקדש. The גמרא objects that מליקה and קמיצה are also very hard, so it rereads the line as 'one of the hardest'. From the ברייתא it proves that the כהן גדול scoops the קטורת a second time inside (חופן וחוזר וחופן). Next comes a new question: if the כהן גדול slaughtered his פר and then died, may a replacement enter with its blood? Two pairs of אמוראים split on how to read 'בפר'. רבי אמי challenges רבי יצחק from the deadline for joining a פסח group, and מר זוטרא challenges from the rule against redeeming a פטר חמור with a slaughtered animal. Both proofs are turned aside as special rules tied to the word 'שה' by פסח, and the גמרא explains how the doubled 'תפדה' widens the donkey law while 'שה' still limits it.

steps.title: How the High Priest moves the incense from the ladle into his hands
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes the hand movements the כהן גדול uses inside קודש הקדשים to get the קטורת from the ladle back into his palms.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he do it? He holds the ladle with the tips of his fingers (some say with his teeth). He pushes it up with his thumb until it reaches between his elbows. Then he tips the incense back into his cupped hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that gives a step-by-step description of a tricky physical task. The כהן גדול must get the קטורת out of the ladle and back into his hands while holding everything himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול enters holding the coal pan (מחתה) in one hand and the ladle of קטורת in the other. Once he puts down the מחתה, he still has to empty the ladle into his palms without dropping anything. The ברייתא explains the method: fingertips (or teeth) on the front of the ladle, the thumb sliding it toward his body, and his elbows used to tip it over.

keyTerms.meaning: How? (opens a description of procedure)
The ladle or spoon that holds the incense
And some say (introduces another opinion)
His elbows
His cupped palms (his two handfuls)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'returning it into his palms' is the key detail. It means the קטורת ends up back in his hands inside, even though he carried it in a ladle. The גמרא builds a conclusion on this detail in step 6.

phrases.english: How does he do it?
He holds the ladle with the tips of his fingers,
and some say with his teeth,
and he pushes it up with his thumb
until it reaches between his elbows,
and then he puts it back into his cupped palms,
phrases.notes: He tips the incense from the ladle back into his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage with a ברייתא describing the procedure inside קודש הקדשים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול moves the קטורת from the ladle back into his own palms inside קודש הקדשים, using his fingertips (or teeth), his thumb, and his elbows.

steps.title: Heaping versus scattering the incense on the coals
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא records two views on how to put the קטורת on the coals: heaped in a pile so the smoke rises slowly, or spread out so it rises quickly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He heaps it in a pile so that its smoke is slow to come up. Some say he spreads it out so that its smoke comes up quickly.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives two opinions on how the קטורת is placed onto the coals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that the קטורת goes onto the coals in the מחתה. They disagree about the method. Heaping it delays the smoke, perhaps so the כהן גדול can leave before the room fills with smoke. Scattering it makes the smoke rise right away.

keyTerms.meaning: He heaps it into a pile
He scatters or spreads it
Its smoke

phrases.aramaic: וְצוֹבְרָהּ, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא עֲשָׁנָהּ שׁוֹהֶה לָבוֹא.
phrases.english: and he heaps it up, so that its smoke is slow to rise.
And some say: he scatters it,
so that its smoke rises quickly.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְצוֹבְרָהּ, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא עֲשָׁנָהּ שׁוֹהֶה לָבוֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the next stage: putting the קטורת on the coals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute over whether the קטורת is heaped (slow smoke) or scattered (quick smoke).

steps.title: The ברייתא calls this the hardest service in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying this handful-taking of the קטורת is 'the' hardest עבודה in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the hardest service in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes with a strong claim. This line sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, the wording claims this is the single hardest עבודה of all. The גמרא is about to question that 'single'.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficult service (a hard Temple procedure)
The Temple

phrases.english: And this is the hardest service in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concluding line of the ברייתא, which the גמרא will now examine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking the handful of קטורת is described as the hardest עבודה in the מקדש.

steps.title: Challenge: aren't pinching and scooping just as hard?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this cannot be the only hardest עבודה, because מליקה and קמיצה are also extremely hard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it only this one and nothing else? But there is pinching the neck of a bird offering! And there is scooping a handful of a meal offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא by naming two other Temple services that are famously hard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מליקה is killing a bird by nipping its neck with the fingernail. קמיצה is scooping exactly a fistful from a מנחה with three fingers, leveled off. Both demand great skill, so calling the קטורת 'the' hardest seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And nothing else?
But there is (introduces a counterexample)
Killing a bird offering by nipping its neck with the fingernail
Scooping a fistful from a meal offering

phrases.english: Is it this one and nothing else?
But there is pinching (of a bird offering)!
And there is scooping (of a meal offering)!

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ הִיא וְתוּ לָא? וְהָא אִיכָּא מְלִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא's final line.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the קטורת handful is THE hardest עבודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexamples: מליקה and קמיצה are also extremely difficult, so this one cannot be uniquely hardest.

steps.title: Answer: it is one of the hardest services
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא to mean the קטורת handful is ONE of the hard services, not the only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: this is a hard service, one of the hard services in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא so it no longer clashes with מליקה and קמיצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The procedure itself does not change. Only the strength of the claim changes, from 'the hardest' to 'among the hardest'. That leaves room for other difficult services too.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a corrected reading)
One of the difficult services

phrases.english: Rather: this is a hard service,
one of the hard services in the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: זוֹ הִיא עֲבוֹדָה קָשָׁה מֵעֲבוֹדוֹת קָשׁוֹת שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading of the wording (narrowing the claim)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא meant the קטורת was the single hardest עבודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is one of several hard services, alongside מליקה and קמיצה.

steps.title: Proof that he scoops a second time inside
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא's description, the גמרא concludes that the כהן גדול scoops the קטורת once outside and again inside (חופן וחוזר וחופן). The conclusion is accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: he scoops, and then scoops again. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the ברייתא about a question raised earlier on the daf, and confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the כהן גדול puts the קטורת back into his palms inside קודש הקדשים. That shows a second handful is taken inside, in addition to the first one taken outside to fill the ladle. Since it was 'hard', this must be a real, deliberate second scooping. So חופן וחוזר וחופן is established.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (draws a conclusion; repeated = 'indeed, conclude so')
He scoops a handful, and scoops again

steps.whatToRemember: The קטורת of יום הכיפורים involves two scoopings: one outside into the ladle, and one inside from the ladle back into his hands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This decides how the procedure must be done. The handful taken outside is not simply carried in and placed down; it is re-scooped inside.

phrases.english: Learn from this: he scoops and then scoops again.
Indeed, learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא just analyzed to settle the procedure.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כהן גדול scoops the קטורת twice: once outside and again inside קודש הקדשים.

steps.title: New question: may a replacement priest use the dead priest's bull blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the כהן גדול slaughtered his פר and then died, may a replacement bring that blood into קודש הקדשים, or must he slaughter a new פר?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if he slaughtered and then died, may another priest go in with its blood? Do we say 'with a bull' means even with the blood of a bull (slaughtered by someone else)? Or perhaps 'with a bull' means a whole bull of his own, and not just its blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a question about a replacement כהן גדול, based on the פסוק 'בזאת יבא אהרן אל הקדש בפר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question depends on how to read the word 'בפר'. If it just means 'with bull blood', any properly slaughtered פר works, even one the first כהן גדול slaughtered. If it means 'with his own bull', the new כהן גדול must slaughter a new פר himself.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (opens a question; step 8 brings the אמוראים' answers)
He slaughtered and died
'With a bull' (ויקרא טז:ג)
Do we say... or perhaps... (the two sides of a question)

phrases.english: A question was raised: if he slaughtered and died,
may another priest enter with its blood?
Do we say: 'with a bull'
means even with the blood of a bull,
or perhaps: 'with a bull'
and not with the blood of a bull (slaughtered by another).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the קטורת discussion closed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the פר's blood stays valid for a replacement כהן גדול, or the replacement must slaughter his own פר.

steps.title: Two pairs of sages split on the bull question
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא and רבי אמי say a new פר is needed. ריש לקיש and רבי יצחק say the existing blood may be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא says: 'with a bull', and not with the blood of a bull. ריש לקיש says: 'with a bull', even with the blood of a bull. רבי אמי says: 'with a bull', and not with the blood of a bull. רבי יצחק says: 'with a bull', even with the blood of a bull.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how the אמוראים answered the question: two pairs of sages take opposite sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא and רבי אמי read 'בפר' strictly: the replacement needs his own bull, so he must slaughter a new one. ריש לקיש and רבי יצחק read it loosely: any valid bull blood is enough, so the replacement may use the blood already slaughtered. The question is answered with a מחלוקת, not a single ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who requires a new bull
An אמורא who allows the existing blood
And not with its blood
And even with its blood

steps.confusionAlert: Every sage here repeats the same word 'בפר'. The difference is only in the tail: 'ולא בדמו' (a new bull is needed) versus 'ואפילו בדמו' (the existing blood is fine).

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina says: 'with a bull'
and not with the blood of a bull,
and Reish Lakish said: 'with a bull'
and even with the blood of a bull.
Rabbi Ami said: 'with a bull'
and not with the blood of a bull;
Rabbi Yitzchak said: 'with a bull'
and even with the blood of a bull.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אוֹמֵר: ״בְּפַר״ — וְלֹא בְּדָמוֹ שֶׁל פַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the אמוראים' answers to the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a מחלוקת. רבי חנינא and רבי אמי require a new bull slaughtered by the replacement. ריש לקיש and רבי יצחק allow him to enter with the existing blood.

steps.title: רבי אמי challenges from the deadline for joining a Pesach group
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי argues against רבי יצחק. By קרבן פסח, people may sign up or withdraw only until the animal is slaughtered. If blood still counts as the animal, the deadline should be the sprinkling of the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי raised an objection to רבי יצחק נפחא (the smith): People may register for a קרבן פסח, and withdraw from it, until it is slaughtered. If you are right that the blood still counts as the animal, the rule should have said 'until the blood is sprinkled'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי attacks the view of רבי יצחק from Step 8, using the laws of signing up for a קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק assumes the blood of a slaughtered animal still counts as the animal itself. If so, the פסח should still 'exist' as long as its blood exists, and people could keep joining until the blood is sprinkled. But the משנה in מסכת פסחים sets the cutoff at שחיטה, which suggests that once the animal is slaughtered, it no longer counts as the same animal.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)
They register (sign up as members of a קרבן פסח group)
They withdraw (literally 'pull their hands away')
Slaughtering the animal
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אמי is the same אמורא who, in Step 8, held that a new פר is needed. Here he is arguing for his own side against רבי יצחק.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami raised an objection to Rabbi Yitzchak the smith:
People may register for it and withdraw their hands from it
phrases.notes: Refers to the group sharing one קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: until it is slaughtered,
and if it is so (that blood still counts as the animal),
it should have said 'until the blood is sprinkled'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי לְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the position of רבי יצחק stated in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption of רבי יצחק and ריש לקיש that a slaughtered animal's blood still counts as the animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If blood equals the animal, the פסח would still exist until זריקה. Yet the sign-up deadline is שחיטה, so the animal seems to 'end' at שחיטה.

steps.title: פסח is different because of a special verse
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that פסח has its own פסוק, 'מהיות משה', which ties membership to the life of the lamb. That rule does not apply to other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is written: 'מהיות משה' (for a lamb). This is read as 'מחיותה דשה': from the life of the lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק defends himself. The פסח rule comes from a special פסוק, not from a general principle about blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'מהיות משה' is read as 'מחיותה דשה', meaning 'while the lamb is alive'. So by פסח the Torah itself sets the cutoff at the animal's death. This is a special rule for פסח. It proves nothing about whether blood normally counts as the animal, so it does not affect the פר of יום כיפור.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there (the case brought as proof has its own reason)
'For a lamb' (שמות יב:ד), the פסוק about joining a פסח group
From the life of the lamb (a play on the words of the פסוק)

phrases.english: It is different there, as it is written:
'for a lamb (mihyot miseh)'
meaning: from the life of the lamb.
phrases.notes: Membership depends on the lamb being alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of רבי אמי by limiting the פסח rule to its own פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (a special פסוק for פסח)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסח deadline shows that blood never counts as the animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסח deadline comes from a special פסוק about the lamb's life, so it says nothing about other קרבנות.

steps.title: מר זוטרא challenges from redeeming a firstborn donkey
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא cites a משנה in מסכת בכורות: a פטר חמור may not be redeemed with a slaughtered animal, only with a שה. This suggests a slaughtered animal no longer counts as a שה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא objected: One may not redeem a firstborn donkey with a calf, a wild animal, a slaughtered animal, a טריפה, a crossbreed, or a כוי. It may only be redeemed with a lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge against רבי יצחק, this time from the laws of redeeming a firstborn donkey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה disqualifies a slaughtered lamb (שחוטה) for redeeming a פטר חמור. It seems that once an animal is slaughtered, it is no longer called a 'שה'. If so, a slaughtered פר should also no longer count as 'the פר', which goes against רבי יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects (raises a challenge from a source)
They redeem (here: a פטר חמור, a firstborn donkey)
An animal that has already been slaughtered
A crossbreed (here: of a sheep and a goat)
A kosher animal whose status is in doubt, between a domestic and a wild animal

phrases.english: Mar Zutra raised an objection:
And one may not redeem (a firstborn donkey)
not with a calf and not with a wild animal
not with a slaughtered animal and not with a fatally injured animal (טריפה)
not with a crossbreed and not with a koy,
but only with a lamb (or kid).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to רבי יצחק, after the first one was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי יצחק and ריש לקיש that a slaughtered animal still keeps its identity as the animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A slaughtered lamb is disqualified as a 'שה' for פדיון. This shows that שחיטה ends the animal's identity.

steps.title: The donkey law is learned from פסח
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that this משנה learns the word 'שה' by פטר חמור from the word 'שה' by פסח. Since a slaughtered animal cannot become a פסח, it also cannot redeem a donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because that תנא learns 'lamb' from 'lamb' by the קרבן פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers מר זוטרא. The disqualification of a slaughtered animal is borrowed from פסח, not based on a general rule about slaughtered animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שה' appears both by פטר חמור and by פסח, so a גזירה שוה links them. A פסח obviously cannot be brought from an animal that is already slaughtered. The donkey law copies this. So again the rule is a special one and does not teach that blood stops counting as the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
He derives (learns one law from another)
The word 'שה' appearing in two places, forming a גזירה שוה

phrases.english: It is different there,
since he derives 'lamb' 'lamb' from the Pesach offering.
phrases.notes: A גזירה שוה between פטר חמור and פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר זוטרא by tying the donkey law back to the special פסח rule from Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (a גזירה שוה to פסח)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A slaughtered animal is disqualified because it no longer counts as a שה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The disqualification is borrowed from פסח through a גזירה שוה, so it proves nothing general.

steps.title: Then the donkey's lamb should need all of the requirements of פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if פטר חמור learns from פסח, its lamb should also have to be male, unblemished, and one year old, like a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as there (by פסח) the animal must be male, unblemished, and a year old, so too here it should have to be male, unblemished, and a year old?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the גזירה שוה it just used. If you copy one rule from פסח, why not copy all of them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה usually brings over the rules of one case to the other. A פסח must be a male, without a blemish, and in its first year. Yet a פטר חמור may be redeemed with any lamb, which seems to break the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, just as there
Male, unblemished, and in its first year (the requirements of a קרבן פסח)
So too here

phrases.english: If so, just as there (by Pesach)
it must be male, unblemished, and a year old,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן זָכָר תָּם וּבֶן שָׁנָה?
phrases.english: so too here it should need to be male, unblemished, and a year old?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן זָכָר תָּם וּבֶן שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the גזירה שוה from Step 12 by asking whether it brings over every פסח requirement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שוה 'שה שה' between פטר חמור and פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is real, all the requirements of פסח should apply to the donkey's lamb. In practice they do not.

steps.title: The repeated 'redeem' widens the law
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the פסוק repeats the word 'redeem' (תפדה... ואם לא תפדה). This repetition widens the law to include animals that would not be fit for a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'you shall redeem', 'you shall (not) redeem'. The repetition comes to include more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A doubled word in the פסוק widens the law, so not every פסח requirement is copied over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubled word 'תפדה' is a רבוי, a signal to include more. It cancels the requirements of male, unblemished, and one year old. The גזירה שוה still disqualifies a slaughtered animal, so the answer to מר זוטרא stands. This also protects רבי יצחק's view that blood normally still counts as the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces a פסוק that settles the question)
You shall redeem (שמות יג:יג)
It broadened (a רבוי that includes more cases)

steps.whatToRemember: So far, both proofs that a slaughtered animal stops counting as 'the animal' have been turned aside as special rules. The פסח rule comes from 'מהיות משה'. The פטר חמור rule is borrowed from פסח, and the repeated 'תפדה' widens it so that not every פסח requirement is copied. This keeps the view of רבי יצחק and ריש לקיש from being refuted, but the גמרא gives no final ruling on the מחלוקת. The next step tests how far the widening goes, and step 16 answers.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא. A proof is turned aside by showing that its case has a special source, so it cannot teach a general rule.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
'you shall redeem', 'you shall redeem' — the repetition broadened it.
phrases.notes: שמות יג:יג: 'תפדה בשה, ואם לא תפדה וערפתו'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 13 with a רבוי from the doubled word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גזירה שוה should bring over all the requirements of פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubled 'תפדה' widens the law, so only some features of פסח apply, such as being alive and being a שה.

steps.title: If the doubled word widens the law, why not include every animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 14: if the doubled 'תפדה' is a widening, it should include all animals, even the ones the משנה excludes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the words 'you shall redeem' and 'you shall redeem' widen the law, then even all of them (calf, wild animal, slaughtered animal) should also be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. If the repeated word 'תפדה' widens the law, why stop at blemished or older lambs? Why not let any animal redeem the donkey?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 used the extra 'תפדה' to include lambs that fail the פסח standards. The challenge is that once you allow a widening, nothing in it seems to set a limit. Then a calf, a חיה, and even a slaughtered animal should all work, and that contradicts the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It widened / included (a רִבּוּי, an extra word that adds cases)
All of them (every excluded category)
Also
A firstborn donkey, which must be redeemed with a שה

phrases.english: If 'you shall redeem', 'you shall redeem' comes to widen,
phrases.notes: Refers to the repetition of the verb in the פסוק about פטר חמור (Step 14).

phrases.english: then even all of them should also be included!
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the calf, the wild animal, the slaughtered animal, and the other cases the משנה excluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the תירוץ of Step 14 by pushing its widening to the extreme.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 14 that the doubled 'תפדה' widens the law of redeeming a פטר חמור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A widening seems to have no built-in limit. If it includes lambs unfit for a פסח, it should include every animal, which would contradict the משנה that excludes a slaughtered animal.

steps.title: The word 'lamb' still has a job, so the widening has limits
steps.stepSummary: The widening cannot include everything, because then the word 'שה' (and its link to פסח) would have no purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what would the word 'lamb' accomplish? (So 'lamb' must still exclude some animals.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. If every animal were included, the word 'שה' in the פסוק would be useless, so the widening must have limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source does its own job. The extra 'תפדה' includes lambs that only fail the פסח standards (female, blemished, older). The word 'שה', learned from פסח, still excludes animals that are not a living שה at all, such as a calf, a חיה, or a slaughtered animal.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reading were correct)
What does it accomplish? What is its purpose?
A teaching that links two topics through a shared word (here 'שה' in פטר חמור and in פסח)

steps.whatToRemember: By פטר חמור the extra 'תפדה' includes lambs that are unfit only for פסח reasons. The word 'שה', linked to פסח, still excludes a slaughtered animal. That exclusion comes from this special link, not from a general rule that slaughter takes away an animal's identity.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think one source cancels the other. The widening and the limit both apply, each to a different kind of case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the attempted proof from the משנה cited by מר זוטרא. Since the exclusion of a slaughtered animal by פטר חמור depends on the special link to פסח, it cannot be used as a general proof about whether an animal keeps its status after slaughter for other laws.

phrases.english: If so, what does 'lamb' accomplish for it?
phrases.notes: If everything were included, the word 'שה' and its link to פסח would teach nothing. So it must still exclude some animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15 by showing the widening must be limited so that the word 'שה' keeps a purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Balancing two sources: a widening limited by a restricting word that must keep its meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubled 'תפדה' includes every animal, even a calf, a wild animal, or a slaughtered one.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תפדה' includes only lambs that fail the פסח standards. 'שה', learned from פסח, still excludes a calf, a wild animal, and a slaughtered animal.
